problem: MLLM-based VLN agents keep explicit semantic memory: textual cognitive maps (e.g., MapNav) or stored history frames (e.g., NaVILA, StreamVLN). This memory loses spatial and geometric information, recomputes the whole history at every step, and grows with trajectory length. Their CLIP-style 2D visual encoders also lack 3D geometric understanding when only RGB is available.
motivation: Navigation is a 3D physical task, yet RGB-only MLLM agents rely on encoders pre-trained on 2D image-text pairs and ignore the 3D cues latent in video (perspective, occlusion, geometry). Adding depth sensors is costly. Feed-forward 3D foundation models like VGGT can recover geometry from RGB alone, but they must reprocess the whole sequence for each new frame (out-of-memory on a 48 GB GPU at 48 frames), which rules them out for streaming navigation. Human hemispheric specialization (semantics vs. spatial cognition) motivates splitting memory into two compact implicit stores.
key_idea: Pair Qwen2.5-VL's semantic vision encoder with a frozen VGGT spatial-geometry encoder, and keep each encoder's history as a fixed-size KV cache (initial 'attention-sink' frames plus a FIFO sliding window). This forms a dual implicit memory that is updated incrementally, without recomputing past frames, and fused into the LLM for low-level action prediction.
insight:
The gain comes from complementary 3D geometric priors, not extra parameters or extra 2D features (R2R-CE val-unseen, no extra data):
- Adding VGGT raises SR/SPL from 47.0/40.9 to 52.8/49.2.
- Adding DINOv2 (47.5/41.5), SigLIP 2 (47.9/41.9) or a randomly initialized VGGT (47.2/40.8) gives almost nothing.

Caching KV instead of re-running VGGT cuts per-frame latency by 69-90% without losing accuracy:
- 8 frames: 82 ms vs 268 ms.
- 32 frames: 149 ms vs 1549 ms, with SR 51.7 vs 51.2.

Performance saturates at a 48-frame window. Dropping the initial-window 'attention sink' KV lowers SR/SPL from 52.8/49.2 to 51.0/47.5. Removing both memories collapses SR to 24.8. A small additive fusion weight (λ=0.2) beats concat (49.4 SR) and slightly beats cross-attention (52.1 SR).
method: Dual encoder: the frozen Qwen2.5-VL ViT gives semantic tokens S_t (2x2 patch-merged). The frozen VGGT encoder plus fusion decoder (prediction head dropped) gives spatial-geometric tokens G_t from RGB only.

Spatial implicit memory: inside VGGT's alternating frame/global attention, the current frame's tokens form queries in global attention. Keys and values are the cached historical KV concatenated with the current frame's KV, so past frames are never re-encoded.

Hybrid incremental update: memory = permanent KV of the first 8 frames ('attention sinks', global anchors) + a FIFO sliding window of the most recent 48 frames. Memory size is fixed regardless of trajectory length.
Semantic implicit memory: the standard KV cache in the Qwen2.5-VL LLM, also restricted to the initial + sliding-window tokens.

Spatial-aware fusion: G_t is 2x2-merged to G'_t to match S'_t, then F_t = S'_t + λ·MLP(G'_t) with a 2-layer MLP and λ=0.2. F_t plus the instruction embedding go to the LLM, which outputs the next action.

Training: one epoch, fine-tuning only the LLM (lr 2e-5) and the projector (lr 1e-5) with both encoders frozen. Uses R2R-CE/RxR-CE, optionally plus 155K ScaleVLN trajectories (~9207K image-action pairs) and 14K DAgger trajectories (~1485K pairs), following StreamVLN.

numbers_note: Full JanusVLN on R2R-CE has SPL 56.8 in Table 1 but 56.6 in the data-ablation table. The HM3D-OVON result is appendix-only, with no description of training setup; whether the model was trained on OVON data is unclear (zero_shot set to false as an assumption). Real-world quantitative results (25 instructions × 3 trials, success within 1 m; +23.6% on spatial tasks vs. the no-spatial-memory variant) and the spatial-term / instruction-length analyses appear only in figures.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen with RGB only, JanusVLN reaches SR 60.5 / SPL 56.8 (NE 4.78). It beats the strongest RGB-only baseline StreamVLN (56.9/51.9) while using about 10.7M vs. ~26.3M external samples, and NaVILA (54.0/49.0). With no external data, JanusVLN* gets 52.8/49.2, beating NaVILA* (49.7/45.5) and StreamVLN* (45.5/41.6). It also beats depth-using methods such as g3D-LF (47.2) and NaVid-4D (43.8). On RxR-CE val-unseen it gets SR 56.2 / SPL 47.5 / nDTW 62.1 vs. StreamVLN's 52.9/46.0/61.9. On HM3D-OVON val-unseen it gets SR 44.9 / SPL 31.7 vs. MTU3D's 40.8/12.1.
limitations: Poor recovery once off the optimal path: compounding errors, and the limited DAgger data is not enough for robust correction.
Overly aggressive / premature stopping, attributed to VGGT features lacking real-world metric scale and hence giving inaccurate distance estimates.

Memory keeps only the initial 8 and most recent 48 frames, so mid-trajectory history is discarded. Evaluation is mainly on VLN-CE (R2R/RxR); real-world tests are small (25 instructions) and run on a remote A10 GPU.
compares_to: ETPNav-era panoramic baselines (CMA, VLN-BERT, Sim2Sim, HPN+DN, GridMM, DreamWalker, Ego2-Map, Reborn)
